This limited Side Quest compares Xubuntu 26.04 LTS and Linux Mint Xfce before a classroom standard is confirmed. Students first complete Power Circuits Questions 1-6. Pilot work does not complete CS01-CS08 early.

## Launch setup {.unnumbered}

- Select two computers matched by model, processor, RAM, storage type, and firmware configuration.
- Prepare identical USB models and use the same USB-port type and procedure.
- Assign technician and recorder roles, then require a role swap.
- Provide an ESD mat or approved grounded work area, correct tools, parts trays, wired input devices, Ethernet, and approved camera access.
- Confirm data ownership and exclude unsafe or privacy-sensitive equipment.

## Required gates {.unnumbered}

Sign before first power after opening. Sign again before students erase, partition, install, replace storage, or move RAM. Students never open or probe a PSU, create a short, invent a fault, force a connector, or move unapproved parts.

Stop for liquid, swollen cells, burnt areas, damaged power hardware, loose metal, sharp damage, smoke, unusual smell, abnormal heat, unstable power, repeated shutdowns, or uncertain data ownership.

## Fair comparison {.unnumbered}

Round 1 places Xubuntu on A and Mint Xfce on B. Round 2 swaps the USB drives. Use the same waiting period before idle-memory readings and the same launch task for the browser, Tinkercad, Inkscape, and VS Code. Do not score live-USB boot time as a computer benchmark.

Use **Pass / Concern / Fail** for individual hardware and usability tests. Use **Green / Yellow / Red** only for the overall machine classification.

## Evidence and decision {.unnumbered}

Look for complete inventory, both crossover rounds, comparable conditions, specific observations, approved photographs, student preference, and an evidence-based recommendation.

The teacher may choose:

- Xubuntu as the classroom standard
- Mint Xfce as the classroom standard
- Lubuntu for weak machines
- additional testing required

Record the decision before any standard installation. The later CS01-CS08 Best Workstation Project begins after Thanksgiving and uses the selected OS to commission, upgrade, benchmark, and recommend a classroom computer.

## Google Classroom posting {.unnumbered}

**Topic:** Side Quests

**Title:** Computer Recovery and OS Comparison

One shared Google Doc per pair. Power Circuits Questions 1-6 must be complete first. Places are limited. Compare both operating systems on matched computers, submit the completed document and approved photos, and stop at every teacher approval gate. Safe evidence determines success even when a machine does not work.

## Official references {.unnumbered}

[Xubuntu releases](https://xubuntu.org/releases/), [Linux Mint downloads](https://linuxmint.com/download.php), [Ubuntu bootable USB guidance](https://documentation.ubuntu.com/desktop/en/latest/how-to/create-a-bootable-usb-stick/), [Apple startup keys](https://support.apple.com/102603), and [Apple Diagnostics](https://support.apple.com/102550).
